en: Most visible matter in the universe is plasma, the fourth state of matter, which makes up glowing stars like our Sun.
The metal gallium melts in your hand because its melting point is 29.76 degrees Celsius, just below normal human body temperature.
Iron rusts much faster in saltwater than in freshwater because dissolved salt accelerates the chemical reaction between iron and oxygen.
Oobleck, a mixture of cornstarch and water, acts like a solid when punched but flows like a liquid when gently poured.
Water is uniquely unusual because its solid state, ice, is less dense than its liquid state, causing ice cubes to float.
Mixing baking soda and vinegar produces carbon dioxide gas, which is the exact same invisible gas you exhale when breathing.
Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide that skips the liquid phase entirely, sublimating directly into a thick, cold, white gas.
Honey has a much higher viscosity than water, meaning its thick molecules resist flowing and sliding past each other very strongly.
Mayonnaise is an emulsion, a special mixture where tiny droplets of liquid oil are permanently suspended in liquid vinegar or lemon juice.
Heating white sugar causes a chemical change called caramelization, transforming it into a completely new brown substance with a different flavor.
Aerogel is a solid material made mostly of trapped air, making it so light that it can rest safely on a flower.
Liquid crystals, used in digital screens, flow like a liquid but have their molecules neatly arranged in organized rows like a solid.
